'''David James Silvester''' (born 26 December 1958) is a British [[Numerical analysis|numerical analyst]]. He has a Chair in Numerical Analysis and is the former Head of [[Applied Mathematics]] in the [[Department of Mathematics, University of Manchester|Department of Mathematics]] at the [[University of Manchester]].<ref name="googlescholar">{{GoogleScholar|-7jBp94AAAAJ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://personalpages.manchester.ac.uk/staff/david.silvester/|title=Homepage: David Silvester|website=personalpages.manchester.ac.uk|access-date=2021-10-24}}</ref><ref name="twitter">{{twitter|davidjsilvester}}</ref>

Silvester was born in [[Dumfries]], but was educated at [[Ysgol Ardudwy]] (Wales) and the [[University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology|University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology (UMIST)]], from which he gained his B.Sc. in Mathematics (1980) and Ph.D. in Numerical Analysis (1983). His Ph.D. thesis (''An Analysis of Finite Element Approximation for Swirling Flow'') was supervised by Ronald Thatcher.<ref name="mathgene">{{MathGenealogy|id=197169}}</ref> He was appointed lecturer in Mathematics at UMIST in 1984, and later promoted to Senior Lecturer and Reader. In 2003 he was promoted to a personal Chair of Numerical Analysis.<ref name="cv">{{Cite web|url=https://personalpages.manchester.ac.uk/staff/david.silvester/webcv.pdf|title=Web CV of David James Silvester|website=personalpages.manchester.ac.uk|access-date=2021-10-24}}</ref> Silvester held visiting positions in the Computer Science Department at [[Stanford University]] in 1991 (as a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Senior Fellow]]) and in 1999, at the [[University of Maryland]] (1994), the [[University of the Littoral Opal Coast]] (2009), and the [[University of Heidelberg]] (2019).<ref>[https://www.mathcomp.uni-heidelberg.de/romberg-program The Distinguished Romberg Guest Professorship]</ref>

Silvester is best known for his work on finite element methods, fast iterative solvers for fluid dynamics, and uncertainty quantification.<ref name="fem">{{cite book|url=https://oxford.universitypressscholarship.com/view/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199678792.001.0001/acprof-9780199678792|title=Finite Elements and Fast Iterative Solvers: With Applications in Incompressible Fluid Dynamics|last1=Elman|first1=Howard|last2=Silvester|first2=David|last3=Wathen|first3=Andy|publisher=Oxford Science Publications|year=2014|isbn=978-0-19-967879-2|location=Second Edition}}</ref> He has more than 65 refereed publications<ref name="googlescholar" /> on topics such as iterative solution of Stokes and Navier–Stokes systems, preconditioning, and error estimation in finite element methods. Silvester's books include ''Finite Elements and Fast Iterative Solvers: With Applications in Incompressible Fluid Dynamics''<ref name="fem"/> and ''Essential Partial Differential Equations'' (co-authored with David F. Griffiths and [[John W. Dold]]).<ref name="pde">{{cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783319225685|title=Essential Partial Differential Equations|last1=Griffiths|first1=David F.|last2=Dold|first2=John W.|last3=Silvester|first3=David J.|publisher=Springer, Heidelberg|year=2015|isbn=978-3-319-22568-5}}</ref>

Silvester has served as the elected President of the UK and Republic of Ireland section of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (2009–2011). He became a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 2023.<ref>[http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2023 SIAM Fellows Class of 2023]</ref> He is on the editorial board of the ''[[Journal of Scientific Computing]]''.<ref name="cv"/>
